coverage_notes: This is a researched starter inventory, not an exhaustive national gazetteer. All seven provinces are represented, but district coverage is selective and uneven.

The inventory emphasizes official tourism-board highlights, UNESCO/Ramsar places and Wikidata-matched destinations. Many rural municipalities, community tourism projects, festivals, homestays, trails, caves, waterfalls and local food experiences remain to be researched.

Wikidata coordinates are stored as published candidate points; they were checked for plausible Nepal bounding-box placement but were not independently cross-checked against an authoritative cadastral/GIS source. Centroids and border features may not represent visitor access points.
Where an attraction spans districts or provinces, administrative_areas records the known wider scope and province/district may be null rather than implying a single jurisdiction.
Traveler ratings, review counts, first-party ratings, budgets, difficulty and most season recommendations are null/empty because no reusable, verifiable source was established.
No image URLs were included. This avoids using unverified location images or assuming a photograph's license/attribution.

ratings_and_images.rating_policy: No external rating or review count was copied. No provider's reuse terms were established. Null does not mean unrated.
ratings_and_images.image_policy: Images are empty until each image is matched to the place and its source, photographer, license and attribution are verified.

destinations.name: Mount Everest
destinations.short_description: The Everest region is a high-altitude landscape of glaciers, icefalls, Sherpa settlements and Himalayan peaks.
destinations.description: Nepal Tourism Board describes the Everest region as a high-altitude mountain and cultural destination reached by trekking, commonly via Lukla. Mount Everest lies on the Nepal–China border; the coordinate is the summit point, not a visitor access point.
destinations.access_info: Nepal Tourism Board describes the usual approach as a flight from Kathmandu to Lukla followed by trekking; a Jiri approach is also described. Check current flights, trail and permit requirements before travel.
data_quality_notes: Summit coordinate is a border point; independently verify the coordinate and the current district/province treatment before using for routing.

destinations.name: Sagarmatha National Park
destinations.short_description: A UNESCO-listed Himalayan protected area encompassing dramatic peaks, glaciers, deep valleys and Sherpa settlements.
destinations.description: UNESCO describes Sagarmatha National Park as a high-mountain landscape that includes Mount Sagarmatha and Sherpa communities. Nepal Tourism Board lists trekking, mountaineering and Sherpa cultural experiences and notes that access commonly begins at Lukla.
destinations.access_info: Nepal Tourism Board lists a flight to Lukla or a bus to Jiri followed by trekking. Check current flights, trail and permit requirements before travel.
data_quality_notes: Best seasons reproduce NTB's March–May and October–November recommendation at broad season level; check current weather and park notices.

destinations.name: Everest Base Camp
destinations.short_description: A high-altitude trekking destination reached through the Everest region.
destinations.description: Nepal Tourism Board describes a multi-day trek from Lukla through the Dudh Koshi valley, Sherpa settlements and Sagarmatha National Park to Everest Base Camp. It notes glaciers, high peaks and Kala Patthar as a viewpoint along the route.
destinations.access_info: Nepal Tourism Board says the commonly used trek starts and ends at Lukla, usually reached by air from Kathmandu. It also mentions a Jiri approach. The source describes a two-week trek; actual durations and access vary. Verify current flights, permits, altitude guidance and trail conditions.
data_quality_notes: No coordinate was added because an authoritative base-camp visitor point was not verified; do not substitute the Everest summit or a generic route point.

destinations.name: Janakpur
destinations.short_description: A Mithila cultural and pilgrimage destination in Nepal's Terai.
destinations.description: Nepal Tourism Board identifies Janakpur as a major religious and cultural destination associated with Sita, temples, ponds, Mithila art and festivals. Janaki Mandir is named as a principal attraction.
destinations.access_info: Nepal Tourism Board reports road travel from Kathmandu (about 390 km/10 hours), intercity buses from Gongabu and flights from Kathmandu of about 40 minutes. Durations are source estimates and should be checked against current services.
data_quality_notes: Destination-level coordinate not supplied because a city-centre point was not independently verified.

destinations.description: Nepal Tourism Board describes Janaki Mandir as a principal pilgrimage attraction in Janakpur, associated with Sita and the city's Vivah Panchami celebrations.
data_quality_notes: The coordinates are a Wikidata point and have not been checked against a survey or current map listing.

data_quality_notes: A group of places rather than one point; individual pond coordinates and present access conditions were not collected.

destinations.short_description: A traditional painting practice associated with Mithila culture and practiced in Nepal and India.
destinations.description: Nepal Tourism Board describes Mithila art as a continuing tradition, often practiced by women, using natural dyes and motifs including nature, geometric patterns and village life.
data_quality_notes: This is a cultural experience, not a single geocoded attraction; a specific community or workshop should be verified before publishing visitor details.

destinations.name: Chitwan National Park
destinations.short_description: A UNESCO-listed lowland park with riverine forests, grasslands, wildlife and Tharu cultural heritage.
destinations.description: UNESCO describes Chitwan as an important Terai ecosystem with river valleys, forest and grasslands, and identifies the park's multi-district extent. Nepal Tourism Board describes jungle safaris, birdwatching and canoe rides among visitor activities.
administrative_areas: Chitwan, Nawalparasi, Parsa and Makwanpur districts (UNESCO listing; district nomenclature requires current-boundary review)
data_quality_notes: The park crosses current provincial/district boundaries; province and district are null to avoid falsely assigning the whole protected area to one jurisdiction. Wikidata returned several linked district statements, deduplicated here.

destinations.name: Ghodaghodi Lake Area
destinations.short_description: A Ramsar-listed oxbow lake and wetland area in Kailali District.
destinations.description: Ramsar describes Ghodaghodi as a shallow oxbow lake with associated marshes, meadows, smaller lakes and ponds, streams and tropical deciduous forest on the lower Siwalik slopes. The wetland is also a religious site and a traditional festival venue for Tharu communities.
data_quality_notes: Coordinates are converted from the Ramsar information sheet (28°41'N, 080°57'E). The sheet's most recent information was published in 2003; verify current local conditions and access.
